source.author: lucan
source.text: Dixerat: at dubium non claro murmure vulgus Secum incerta fremit: pietas patriique penates Quamquam caede feras mentes animosque tumentes Frangunt; sed diro ferri revocantur amore Ductorisque metu.
source.text_original: Dixerat: at dubium non claro murmure vulgus / Secum incerta fremit: pietas patriique penates / Quamquam caede feras mentes animosque tumentes / Frangunt; sed diro ferri revocantur amore / Ductorisque metu.
source.text_english: He had spoken: but the crowd, in uncertain murmuring and not with loud outcry, mutters to itself in doubt: piety and their native household gods, though by slaughter they break savage minds and swelling spirits, are broken; but they are called back by a dreadful love of the sword and by fear of the leader.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: tu sola animos mentesque peruris, Gloria; te viridem videt immunemque senectae Phasidis in ripa stantem iuvenesque vocantem.
reuse.text_original: tu sola animos mentesque peruris, / Gloria; te viridem videt immunemque senectae / Phasidis in ripa stantem iuvenesque vocantem.
reuse.text_english: you alone, Glory, burn up minds and hearts; the Phasis sees you standing on its bank, green and free from old age, and calling the young men.
